messages:
Maya (PM): quick sync — we need a compact rollout plan for the model-routing flag that covers hosted/dedicated/private. customer ask: region pinning + failover to cheaper variant. scope tradeoffs?
Jon (Eng): agree. propose two-phase: canary (1%), regional ramp (10/33/100), then global. canaries should target low-traffic tenants and a dedicated canary pool.
Priya (SRE): +1. canary pool needs isolated infra so noisy neighbors don't skew metrics. I'll carve out 2 GPU nodes per region for the first week.
Ken (Solutions): heads-up: Customer-AC wants VPC-only for initial opt-in. we'll need a private key rotation step before opt-in. also they want SLA language for fallback latency.
Lina (QA): test plan: smoke, perf, and semantic-regression on canonical prompt set. suggest automated daily evals during ramp and a one-off manual check at each 10% step.
Maya (PM): good. what are launch kill-criteria? need clear numbers everyone agrees on.
Jon (Eng): suggested kill if 95th latency increases > 120% vs baseline OR token-error-rate > 0.8% OR quality delta on eval > 1.5% (absolute) for 3 consecutive hours.
Priya (SRE): add: if canary CPU/GPU OOM or KV cache evictions spike > 3x baseline => immediate rollback. also circuit-breaker to route traffic to fallback variant.
Ken (Solutions): fallback variant should be cheaper quantized model with same token schema. legal ok with that.
Lina (QA): scheduling: canary run 48 hours minimum with hourly metric checks, then each ramp step 24 hours minimum with rolling checks. A/B duration for fidelity experiments: 7 days.
Maya (PM): telemetry contract (what we need): per-tenant latency histogram, tokens/generated, model-version, route, error types, quality-score event, canary-flag-state. needs to be shipped before deploy.
Jon (Eng): I'll add the flag config to infra repo. proposed flag YAML snippet:

```yaml
flag: model_routing_v2
phases:
  - name: canary
    percent: 1
    tenants: ["internal-qa", "low-traffic-cohort"]
    regions: ["us-west-2"]
  - name: regional_ramp
    percent: 10
    regions: ["us-west-2", "eu-west-1"]
  - name: global
    percent: 100
```

Jon (Eng): flag rollout will include automatic fallback mapping in case of error type match. mapping table will be in the same file.
Priya (SRE): I'll add alerts: canary_lag > 200ms_p50_delta, canary_error_rate > 0.5%, kv_evictions_rate. Pager on high severity.
Ken (Solutions): customer communication: ETA for opt-in and KMS rotation? we need a 48h window for legal and security signoff.
Maya (PM): timeline proposal: PRs and telemetry by 2026-03-29, canary deploy 2026-04-01, ramping during April week 1-2, full by April 15 (contingent on gates).
Lina (QA): test ownership: Eng to run automated smoke, QA to validate semantic checks and nightly evals. I'll create the test checklist.
Jon (Eng): action items: add flag PR + mapping, wire telemetry events, add fallback route code. ETA: PR today, review tomorrow.
Priya (SRE): action items: allocate canary pool, add Prometheus rules, and create runbook for manual rollback.
Ken (Solutions): action items: send customer opt-in email template and KMS checklist.
Maya (PM): decision: go with the two-phase plan + the kill-criteria Jon suggested, with Priya's infra checks as hard gates. I'll update the rollout doc and notify launch room.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled by deploy-bot for 2026-04-01 16:00 UTC — canary flag will be toggled to 1% in us-west-2 after smoke run :rocket:
Ken (Solutions): noted — will block opt-ins until KMS rotation completes.
Lina (QA): will run initial smoke at +15min post-deploy, will post results here.
Maya (PM): thanks all — I'll post the updated checklist and owner table. tagging next steps: @Jon (Eng) @Priya (SRE) @Lina (QA) @Ken (Solutions). :thumbsup:
Jon (Eng): working on the PR now.
Priya (SRE): infra is provisioned — will share node IDs in the rollout doc.
Lina (QA): checklist created and linked in doc review.
Maya (PM): wrap-up: owners and signoffs required before canary: Eng PR merged, telemetry live, SRE infra ready, QA checklist green, legal/kms ok for customer opt-ins.
